newsitem.title: JAPAN: Guatemala's Anacafe sees coffee price correction.
newsitem.headline: Guatemala's Anacafe sees coffee price correction.

text.p: The president of Guatemala's National Coffee Association (Anacafe) said in Tokyo on Thursday that world coffee prices are likely to see a downward correction in the near term following a rally since late last year.

"Open interest (in the world coffee futures markets) is extremely high and I think world coffee prices will have a downward correction soon," Julio Arrivillaga told Reuters after a news conference here.
On Wednesday, the most-active March coffee futures on the New York Coffee, Sugar and Cocoa Exchange (CSCE) surged to a 15-month high of 147.80 cents per lb.
Arrivillaga also said the recent export curbs agreed to by the Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) would have only a short-term impact on world prices.
"I think the ACPC agreement will have a short-term impact on the world market, but I'm very doubtful about its long-term impact," he told reporters.
The ACPC recently agreed to cut an additional 1.3 million 60-kg bags of exports in the first half of 1997.

Asked about Guatemala's production costs, he said, "It's difficult to tell the break-even point for Guatemala coffee producers, because it depends on the size (of the plantation), but the average break-even point is around 130 cents a pound."
